new_pinned_packet.content: Lemma K2: with two crossing partitions, B is in configuration (I), (II), or (III). Proposition F: for every two-prime |A| = 2^a q^b, A is equidistributed mod 2q. Corollary F1: for q in {5,11}, (III) is excluded by the seeds, so every fibre of B lies in one coset of 2qZ_N, with parity a function of one residue and q-residue a function of the other; for q=3, (III) forces B into the evens union 1+3Z.

new_written_lemma_recorded_here_not_prom.statement: For q in {5,11} and |A| = 4q (|A| in {20,44}), every class mod 2q of A is a pair whose two elements are congruent mod 4q^2.
new_written_lemma_recorded_here_not_prom.proof: By Corollary F1 every fibre is b_y + 2qY_y. Proposition F makes each class mod 2q a pair {a_j, a_j + 2q s_j}, and Y_y is a common complement of the pairs {0, s_j} in Z_(N/2q), so Y_y + 2s_j = Y_y for all j. Hence B is periodic under H = <4qg> x {0}, where g = gcd(s_j, N/2q) depends only on A. If g is odd, H has the full 2-part 2^(v-2) of |B_y|; if q does not divide g, the full q-part q^(w-1). Either way the descent gives a quotient FACT solution with 2 or q not dividing |B-bar|, contradicting 330 | |B-bar|. So 2q divides every s_j.
